title: Blasts destroy rock that was never unsupported
question: The engine is currently breaking rock that had real support — it just hadn't found out yet. Converging the support field leaves 25,470 MORE cells standing after one charge. Before I build the shipping version: is the amount of collapse you get after a blast today about right, or already more than you want? If it's about right, this fix will make blasts visibly LESS destructive and I should give some of it back on purpose.
context_md:
**No A/B image — this is a "how much should break" question and the number is the claim.** The picture is one cascade run to rest, so you can judge the amount against something.

**What is going on.** The support field corrects itself reactively, one cell per five frames, and after a charge that correction never catches up. Measured eleven thousand frames after a single radius-20 blast at the shipped 8192x2560, with the world materially still: **1,464 cells per frame are still raising their distance**, and roughly 1 site in 2,000 ever reaches the load model. Every value written on the way up is wrong, and a cell that climbs past its own span **breaks and takes its neighbours with it** before the true value arrives.

You can see it in the sheet below. `what came off` is flat at 202 cells across all five tiles — nothing new is actually moving — while `unsupported` climbs 323 → 503 → 683. That climb is the bug.

**The measurement.** Two 6,000-frame runs, identical except that one converges the field once at frame 3,000:

| | body cells standing at the end | mean frame | frames over budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| today | 19,471,238 | 42.27 ms | 96.9% |
| **converged** | **19,496,708** | **33.29 ms** | **85.3%** |

So converging is worth ~14 ms of a ~40 ms frame **and** 25,470 cells of rock that should never have fallen.

**Why I am asking instead of just building it.** It changes a blast two ways at once — less total collapse, and it arrives sooner, because part of the delay you see today is literally the wavefront crawling. `CHAIN_WINDOW_FRAMES` is 600 frames of deliberate generosity built around that crawl. If today's blast already feels too destructive, this is a straight win. If it feels right, a performance fix should not quietly retune your game.

Nothing has shipped: the machinery is in PR #68, off by default.
